Glance at a Multiple-Factor CFA Fit

Source: R/fa_confirmatory.R
glance.dmar_fa_confirmatory.Rd

Returns a one-row data.frame of model-level summaries from a fa_confirmatory table, in the column convention used by the broom ecosystem.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dmar_fa_confirmatory'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A dmar_fa_confirmatory object returned by fa_confirmatory.

...

Unused.

Value

A one-row data.frame with columns chi_square, df, p_value, cfi, tli, rmsea, rmsea_low, rmsea_high, srmr, AIC, BIC, logLik, and the columns that say what produced them, so that rows of different fits can be stacked and still read: estimator; missing, the missing data method of the fit ("listwise", "pairwise", "fiml", "two_stage", "robust_two_stage", or "none" for a covariance matrix); test, the statistic in chi_square ("standard", "scaled", or a two-stage statistic); fit_indices, the version of cfi, tli, and rmsea ("robust", "scaled", or "standard"); and rmsea_ci_level, the level of the RMSEA interval (rmsea_conf_level, 0.90 by default, where the conf_level column of tidy() is the level of the parameter intervals). After two-stage estimation logLik is the complete data normal log likelihood at the EM estimates and AIC and BIC are the two-stage criteria of Lai (2021), comparable only with two-stage fits of the same variables, not with a FIML or listwise row; and the difference of two rows' chi_square or logLik is not a chi square test of nested models under a scaled or two-stage statistic (lavaan::lavTestLRT() on output = "fit" gives the right one).

References

Lai, K. (2021). Using information criteria under missing data: Full information maximum likelihood versus two-stage estimation. Structural Equation Modeling, 28(2), 278–291. doi:10.1080/10705511.2020.1780925
